title: Treasury Standard: Mailing Charge on Replacement Capital Credit Checks
content:
# Mailing Charge on Replacement Capital Credit Checks

**Treasury standard — Capital Credits (Patronage Capital).** The mailing charge of a replacement follows how its checks went astray:

1. where the account's voided checks include at least **2** returned undeliverable, the replacement goes by certified mail and **$6.95** is deducted;
2. where they include a check reported lost and fewer than 2 returned undeliverable, **$3.50** is deducted for the stop-payment notice;
3. otherwise no mailing charge is deducted.

The charge is deducted from the face of the replacement and recorded among the charges deducted from it. The reasons are read from the void entries on the capital account: stale-dated, lost or returned undeliverable.

## Decision table

| Voids returned undeliverable | Voids reported lost | Mailing charge |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | any | $6.95, certified mail |
| 0 or 1 | 1 or more | $3.50, stop-payment notice |
| 0 or 1 | none | none |

## Hypothetical cases

| Void history on the account | Mailing charge |
|---|---|
| one stale-dated void | none |
| one void returned undeliverable | none |
| one lost, one returned undeliverable | $3.50 |
| two returned undeliverable | $6.95 |
| two returned undeliverable and one lost | $6.95 |
